is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles funestus and Anopheles gambiae s.l. (page 3, 4).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for GSTe2 L119F (page 5, 7, 8), A296S-RDL (page 5, 9), and Vgsc L1014F (kdr-w) (page 5, 7).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Table 2 (page 8) provides genotype counts for L119F-GSTe2 in mated males, unmated males, mated females, and indoor collected females. Table 3 (page 9) provides genotype counts for A296S-RDL.

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in Tibati, Cameroon (page 3, 4).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical research article reporting original field and laboratory data.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study was conducted in Tibati, Adamawa Region, Cameroon (page 3).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections took place in February and March 2018 (page 4).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes new field collections and experiments conducted in 2018.

supplement.evidence: All necessary genotype counts and bioassay data are provided in the main text tables and figures.

assessment.summary: This study investigated the impact of the L119F-GSTe2 metabolic resistance marker on the mating competitiveness of male Anopheles funestus in Tibati, Cameroon. The study also characterized the insecticide resistance profile of the local An. funestus and An. gambiae s.l. populations using WHO bioassays and genotyping for resistance markers.
